text:
maria: Quick ask — can someone run a perf bench comparing streaming+funcall when we emit structured JSON (schema validation step) vs plain streaming funcall? I think the serializer tweak in PR #8423 added ~10-15% overhead on p95. Need concrete numbers for the PR and release notes.

josh: I can run it. Which model and sequence lengths do you want? Also cold vs warm? :eyes:

maria: gptj-16k-quant (closest to current perf), seq 512 and 2048. Please include cold-start and warm runs, batch sizes 1 and 4. Capture p50/p95 and tokens/sec.

akash: Also test with --kv-cache=true and false. The serializer change touched the postprocess path that runs even if kv cache hits skip some steps.

sam: FYI I have an older run (before PR) for streaming+funcall without structured output:

```
mode: streaming-funcall
seq:512 batch:1 p50:28ms p95:120ms tps:420 tokens/s
seq:2048 batch:1 p50:120ms p95:520ms tps:140 tokens/s
```

Use that as baseline.

nina: I'll kick off the bench now. Command I use: 

```
./bench/run.sh --model gptj-16k-quant \
  --seq 512,2048 --modes streaming,streaming-funcall,streaming-funcall-json \
  --iters 50 --batch 1,4 --kv-cache true,false
```

bench-bot: Job queued: job/6791 by nina (params recorded).

maria: please make sure to also set --sample-rate=0.1 so we collect profiler samples for the high tail. and include --no-warmup false (i.e., do warmup).

nina: updated command and started job/6791. ETA ~12m. I'll paste quick summary when done.

[~10m later]

nina: job/6791 finished. Quick summary (warm runs, batch=1, kv-cache=true):

```
mode: streaming                seq:512  p50:30ms  p95:138ms  tps:405  overhead: +8.0% vs baseline
mode: streaming-funcall        seq:512  p50:33ms  p95:160ms  tps:380  overhead: +14% vs baseline
mode: streaming-funcall-json   seq:512  p50:40ms  p95:220ms  tps:320  overhead: +28% vs baseline

mode: streaming                seq:2048 p50:125ms p95:540ms tps:135 overhead: +3% vs baseline
mode: streaming-funcall        seq:2048 p50:140ms p95:610ms tps:120 overhead: +12% vs baseline
mode: streaming-funcall-json   seq:2048 p50:160ms p95:780ms tps:95  overhead: +34% vs baseline
```

Notes: structured JSON path adds extra validation + stringification on the main thread. p95 impact larger for higher seq.

josh: ouch — json path is expensive. Is validation synchronous? We could shift to async validation or stream-validate. akash, can you profiler the decoder hot loop while a funcall-json run is happening?

akash: On it. I'll rerun with `--profiler=cpu` and attach flame for the p95 window. If the cost is in serializer, optimization options: incremental emitter, precompiled schema, or move to background worker.

[~15m later]

akash: profiler shows ~65% of extra time in `emit_structured_output()` and another ~15% in memory copies during string concat. Attached small flame (pasted snippet):

```
emit_structured_output (65%)
  -> format_field (30%)
  -> validate_schema (20%)
  -> join_parts (15%)
```

I can try a fast path that skips validation for known-good templates which should cut validation cost entirely.

maria: That would be ideal. For PR #8423 we should include numbers and suggested mitigations. Nina/Josh — can you run the same job with a precompiled-template flag? e.g., `--structured-fastpath=true`?

nina: yes will queue job/6792 with fastpath.

bench-bot: Job queued: job/6792 by nina.

nina: job/6792 done, quick numbers (seq512 batch1 kv-cache=true):

```
streaming-funcall-json (fastpath) seq:512 p50:36ms p95:180ms tps:350 overhead: +18% vs baseline
```

Better but still ~18%. Fastpath removed validation but still does formatting work.

josh: OK. For release notes we should call out ~25-35% p95 overhead in worst-case (large seqs) and propose mitigations: precompiled templates, background validation, or opt-in structured output.

maria: Agree. I'll update PR #8423 with these numbers and add an opt-in flag behind API. Also will ping docs to mark structured-output as alpha.

sam: Quick code-review note: pls add a metric `structured_emit_ms` to runtime counters so we can track in prod.

maria: Good call. Nina akash, can you add that to the instrumented path in the followup?

akash: Yep I'll add and submit a tiny PR.

nina: pushed benchmark snippets to the thread and attached raw logs to the ticket.

maria: thanks everyone. If anyone sees >30% regressions on other models, flag it here. Closing this thread. :thumbsup:
